title: Brown Sugar Cinnamon Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Warm brown sugar cupcakes with a baked in cinnamon ribbon, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a coffee cake and a cupcake had a baby. Brown sugar batter gets a ribbon of cinnamon sugar swirled through the middle before baking. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen three times to get the swirl to stay put instead of sinking to the bottom. The frosting is simple vanilla buttercream with a cinnamon swirl piped right into it, so every bite gets a little spice. It is a classic recipe with a cozy twist, good for fall but honestly good any time of year. You do not need special tools for the swirl. A butter knife and a light hand are all it takes to get that pretty ribbon look without deflating the batter.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and brown sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla.
Add flour mixture and milk in three additions, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
In a small bowl, stir together the swirl brown sugar and cinnamon until it looks like wet sand.
Fill each liner about one third full with batter. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of cinnamon swirl mix on top of each.
Add another layer of batter to fill liners two thirds full, then use a toothpick to swirl the cinnamon mix gently through the batter.
Bake 17 to 19 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth and pale, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating after each.
Mix in vanilla, cinnamon, and heavy cream. Beat 2 more minutes until fluffy.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe frosting on top in a swirl pattern. Dust with a pinch of cinnamon if you like.
tips: Do not skip the cool down time before frosting. Warm cupcakes melt buttercream fast.
Layer the batter and swirl mix in two additions so the cinnamon stays in the middle, not at the bottom.
Room temperature eggs and butter mix smoother and trap more air, which makes a lighter crumb.
For a stronger cinnamon flavor in the frosting, add another 1/4 teaspoon, but taste as you go.

faq.question: Why did my cinnamon swirl sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: This happens when all the batter goes in first and the swirl mix sits on top before baking. Layer the batter in two parts with the cinnamon mix in between, then swirl gently with a toothpick.

faq.question: Can I make the batter ahead and bake later?
faq.answer: Mix the batter and refrigerate up to 4 hours in a covered bowl. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before filling liners so it bakes evenly.

faq.question: Can I use dark brown sugar instead of light?
faq.answer: Yes, dark brown sugar works and gives a deeper molasses flavor. The cupcakes will taste slightly richer but the texture stays the same.

faq.question: Why is my frosting swirl not holding its shape?
faq.answer: Your butter may be too soft or your kitchen too warm. Chill the frosting for 10 minutes before piping, and use a large open star tip for the best hold.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring coffee cake comfort into a handheld treat. The cinnamon ribbon inside is the fun surprise, and the frosting ties it all together with a warm vanilla and cinnamon finish.
